reviews.review: In The Name Of The Emperor. CLEANSE, PURGE, KILL!
love the atmosphere of this game. Wish there was a sequel

If you've played Gears of War, the mechanics and gameplay will be very familiar to you, although with less use of cover and a lot more melee combat (more on that in a bit). Nothing is overly complicated, and the controls allow you to seamlessly switch between melee and ranged attacks, which maybe isn't the most realistic, but supports the Doom-esque "just run in there and f*ck everything up" play-style the game seems to encourage, over the careful advance/cover/fire/advance tactics required from most shooter games. Some areas will force you to strategize (like the area right before the final boss fight, oh man that took a lot of attempts) and are satisfying to beat, but overall this is more of the kind of game you'd play if you had a long day at work and just want to destroy a bunch of aliens without thinking too hard.

Pros: Excellent atmosphere and sound design that really captures the 40k universe better than any other 40k game I've played (as much as I love DOW). You're supposed to be a 7' tall transhuman super soldier that weighs over half a ton in your massive suit of armor, and your main weapon is essentially a .75-caliber fully automatic rocket-propelled grenade launcher. The game does a great job of portraying this - every step your character takes shakes the ground, every shot you fire is satisfyingly loud and destructive. Regular-sized human enemies can basically explode if you barrel into them at a full sprint. Speaking of which, the gore is just enough to be satisfying without being gratuitous or unbelievable. The melee combat is also sufficiently weighty, and has just the right amount of variety without getting too into complicated combos and what not. 

Cons: The story is meh. The Ultramarines are arguably the most boring of all the space marine chapters, and the plot is essentially the usual "orks are attacking, oh no there's something else going on here, *gasp* its Chaos!" that you might expect if you've played 40k games before. Also, the variety of enemies is a bit lacking. Once chaos showed up I was looking forward to fighting demons, but there's only one type of demon and everyone else is traitor guardsmen and chaos marines with assorted weaponry, with a couple of psykers thrown in, but they act more like stationary turrets than interesting enemies. 

Overall I really enjoyed this game. Its fun and engaging but not complicated and doesn't require much brainpower, which is sometimes exactly the kind of game I'm looking for. There's a good variety of weapons, melee attacks, and special abilities, enough to keep things interesting without getting overly complicated. There wasn't a lot of variety in the environment/scenery but it changed often enough to not get tiring. The levels are broken up with some 'alternative' sections where you might be manning a gun turret shooting down enemy flyers, or sections where you get a jump jet and thunderhammer and get to just go to town flying around the map smashing enemies to bits, and no section overstays its welcome. It doesn't really have a lot of 'replay value' once you've smashed your way through the campaign (about 8 or 9 hours), but pick this game up on sale and I'd say its well worth the money.
